definition: Approbation means praise or official approval.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word approbation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know approbation should be able to work it out from your sentence.

Praise is far milder than approbation — any warm word, from anyone, about anything; it needs no title and no letterhead, while approbation is a verdict from someone entitled to judge.
Worship goes further than approbation — approbation approves with judgment still switched on; worship has stopped judging altogether.

Applause is a crowd's noisy, immediate yes — hands together in the moment, nobody weighing anything. Approbation is the considered, often official approval pronounced by someone entitled to judge, after the merits have been weighed. The crowd claps on the spot; a board deliberates first and only then grants its approbation.

Esteem is steady high regard held over time — a standing opinion of someone's worth that nobody needs to announce. Approbation is the moment approval is actually pronounced: a verdict delivered, a stamp given. You can hold a colleague in esteem for years without once putting the approbation in writing.

In 1761, a young clockmaker named Ester Vane submitted her marine timekeeper to the Board of Longitude, the panel with sole power to certify instruments for the navy.
The Board did not clap and did not hurry.
Its examiners ran the clock through a six-week sea trial, logged its drift each noon, and questioned her about every spring and screw.
Sailors who saw the device loved it at once, and their letters praised its steadiness in rough water.
But affection moved nothing.
Only the Board's approbation could put her clock aboard a king's ship, and the Board granted it slowly: a signed certificate, read into the minutes, eleven months after she first knocked.
Ester framed the certificate.
The letters from sailors she kept in a drawer.
